transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-08 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Maya (Kepler Eng Mgr), Arjun (Kepler ML Eng), Liam (Kepler SRE), Nadia (Kepler Product)

Summary (auto): Reviewed POC throughput numbers, agreed on next steady-state test at higher concurrency; discussed batching window and backpressure; action items captured.

[00:00] Sofia: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, do you all see the deck i shared? i put the latest numbers in the sheet, link in the chat - drive/kepler/pilot-results.csv
[00:12] Maya: yep can see it, thanks. quick context, we ran the last overnight with concurrency 32, p50 around 42ms, p95 jumped to 1.2s during the 1am spike, looking to tighten the tail.
[00:30] Ethan: okay great, so the main levers here are batch window, concurrency, and queue depth plus kv cache behavior. last run used 40ms batch window and max inflight 32, is that right?
[00:45] Arjun: correct, and we saw frequent k-v cache cold misses during scale up, probably due to new prompt prefixes. that plus occasional kernel thrash on the GPU.
[00:58] Priya: small clarif, when you say kernel thrash do you mean context swap between quantized and fp16 kernels? sometimes the runtime falls back.
[01:07] Arjun: yeah it's noisy, sometimes the model drops into slower path when sequence lengths spike.
[01:15] Liam: and our burst pattern at 00:55 had lots of small requests which created lots of micro-batches, that blew up queueing.

[05:10] Sofia: what we're proposing — and ethan can walk through the config — is to try higher concurrency (48) but shorten the batch window to ~20ms and cap queue depth to 150, that should increase throughput while keeping per-token latency sane.
[05:28] Ethan: right, the continuous batching model means we accept slightly smaller batches but more parallelism. tradeoff is GPU saturation; we want to avoid pushing to the point where p95 climbs. so we will monitor token admission and trust the runtime's backpressure.
[05:46] Nadia: is there an automated fallback if latency creeps up? we don't want production errors.
[05:52] Ethan: yes, we can enable a fallback policy: if p95 > 900ms for more than 2 minutes, route to a cheaper smaller model variant or reduce concurrency on the pool; Redwood's control plane can do canary fallback.
[06:03] Maya: okay good. also security question — can you sign our staging allowlist?
[06:08] Sofia: yes we'll provide an IP list. i'll also send SOC2 docs.

[12:00] Arjun: last night's trace shows a periodic spike correlated with cache thrash. i can upload the 30-minute trace, but the key is kv cache warmup — initial requests after a cold start are super slow.
[12:20] Ethan: do you have typical prefix reuse stats? like how much of your traffic benefits from prefix caching?
[12:28] Arjun: roughly 65% of calls share the same initial 120 tokens, then branching. so warmup matters.
[12:36] Priya: we'll prioritize pre-warming the KV cache on test runs; Ethan will send a script to generate warmup traffic to populate hot keys before steady-state run.

[18:50] Liam: question on observability — we'll need per-route token-level breakdown and flamegraphs for the 3-hour run. can the console capture that?
[18:58] Ethan: yes the Console will export per-request latencies, token counts, cost per-token; we can also provide flamegraphs and kernel-level traces from the agent. please confirm retention expectations.
[19:10] Liam: 30 days is fine for the pilot.

[24:00] Sofia: quick review of results from the small smoke test: concurrency 40, batch window 30ms, saw throughput increase 1.6x vs baseline but p95 rose to ~780ms, so we want to see if 48 + 20ms keeps p95 < 900ms.
[24:20] Maya: also note cost sensitivity — pricing matters, if burst capacity costs double then we need to evaluate cost per unit throughput.
[24:32] Sofia: understood. i'll include burst pricing options in the doc.

[30:00] Ethan: technical note — we'll enable continuous batching mode with adaptive batching window that targets 20ms under steady load; queue depth cap at 150 and inflight concurrency goal 48. backend will throttle admissions if queue hits 120 to avoid head-of-line lat spikes.
[30:18] Arjun: sounds good, do you expect any model quality regressions from batching? we've seen truncation problems when we push larger micro-batches.
[30:28] Ethan: no quality change expected; batching is at token-chunk granularity and doesn't coalesce prompts. truncation would be from sequence-length enforcement; we'll keep max seq high for your workload.

[35:00] Sofia: recap: Redwood runs 3-hour steady-state at 48 concurrency, adaptive 20ms batching, queue cap 150; Kepler provides request trace and enables staging IP allowlist; deliverables: perf logs, flamegraphs, security docs, pricing. follow-up 2026-07-14
[35:24] Maya: thanks everyone. small ask — can you also include an A/B where fallback goes to smaller quantized model to compare unit cost?
[35:33] Ethan: yes we'll include the fallback comparison in the run.
[35:40] Sofia: great. any last questions?
[36:00] Nadia: none from product.
[36:05] Liam: all good.
[36:12] Arjun: i'll upload the traces after this call.
[36:20] Sofia: perfect. thanks, we'll follow up by email with the timeline.
[36:30] (call ends)
